title: The seam: how a tight end gets open up the middle (and why the Giants' tight end had 127 yards)
html:
Why this lesson now: the Film Room mirror (football-brief, branch film-room) was checked this run. It still holds one logged game file (data/games/gmum7mktl1wy3.json, "Eagles at Bears, Week 3", no snaps logged) and no review files. The backup source (football-film-room, branch "data") couldn't be read: "GitHub access to this repository is not enabled for this session." So there's no new miss of yours to fix, and no snap of yours this connects to yet. It's a new concept, tied to Thursday night's game and Lesson 52.

The big idea: zone defenses have soft spots between defenders.One of the biggest is up the middle, between two deep safeties. Coaches call it the seam.A tight end is often the player who runs there. He's bigger than a cornerback and faster than most linebackers.

Labels A–D match the steps below. White = offense, yellow = defense. Dashed white line = the throw.

  1. A · The release. The tight end lines up next to the right tackle. At the snap he runs straight up the field.At first it looks like he might block. That buys him a step.
  2. B · Past the linebacker. In zone coverage (Lesson 5), a linebacker guards a short area, about 5 to 10 yards deep.Once the tight end runs past him, the linebacker has to let him go. Now he's in nobody's area for a moment.
  3. C · The seam. In Cover 2 (Lesson 8), two safeties each guard half of the deep field.The space between them, up the middle, is the soft spot. Each safety has to cover a lot of grass to get there.
  4. D · The throw. The QB has to throw before a safety closes, about 2.5 to 3 seconds after the snap.A catch here is usually 15 to 25 yards. That's a medium-to-deep throw on the route tree (Lesson 52).

Thursday night, for real: the Giants' leading receiver wasn't a wide receiver. Tight end Isaiah Likely caught 9 passes for 127 yards and a TD. Malik Nabers had 5 for 44.

Washington's tight end Ben Sinnott caught 4 for 42 and a TD too. Tight ends caught 2 of the game's 4 TD passes.

Why it matters for bets: the brief's McCarthy lean expected short throws in the rain. But the middle of the field was open, and McCarthy threw for 293. When you judge a QB yards prop, check whether his tight end is healthy and whether the defense plays two deep safeties. That's a lesson the brief is using for Saturday's Arch Manning lean.

In your drill: when you log "P", watch the tight end. If he runs straight up the field and you see two safeties deep, guess "seam." If he stays in to block, guess a quick throw or play-action.

Real examples to watch: tonight, Illinois at UCLA (6:00 p.m. PT, FOX). Saturday, Minnesota at Penn State (4:00 p.m. PT, FS1): Penn State's tight ends get 11.6 targets a game, the most in the Big Ten (BetMGM). Count how many of those go up the middle.

Video: search YouTube for "tight end seam route vs Cover 2" and "Isaiah Likely Giants Commanders highlights."

Practice it in Football Camp → (Station 3: Safeties & coverages)

o: The gap between the center and a guard
The open space up the middle, between the two deep safeties
The area behind the line where screens are thrown
quiz.w: In Cover 2 each safety guards one deep half. The middle, between them, is the soft spot a tight end can run to.

quiz.q: Why can a tight end run past a linebacker in zone coverage?
o: Linebackers aren't allowed to touch receivers
The linebacker guards only a short area, so he has to let the tight end go
The tight end starts behind the linebacker
quiz.w: In zone, the linebacker covers an area about 5 to 10 yards deep. Once the tight end is past it, he's between defenders.

quiz.q: Thursday, who led the Giants in receiving yards?
o: Isaiah Likely, 9 catches for 127 and a TD
quiz.w: Tight end Isaiah Likely had 127 yards. That's a big reason McCarthy threw for 293 and the Under 225 lean lost.

quiz.q: In your drill, the tight end runs straight up the field and there are two deep safeties. What's a good guess?
o: A seam throw to the tight end
quiz.w: Tight end releasing upfield plus two deep safeties is the classic seam look.
